body.statement: There exists a positive selected law on two binary observed variables and a one-parameter family of finite SCMs with constant moment vector \(\zeta(M)\) such that the SCM has a common-source bidirected edge for every interior parameter value and loses that edge at both boundary values. Therefore, preservation of \(\zeta(M)\) alone does not preserve exact graph legality, although the boundary moment vector has a distinct legal lift.
body.justification: The proposition rules out the tempting but invalid inference from Carathéodory moment preservation to exact-edge preservation.
body.gap: Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe preserve observed behavior, not functional essentiality; this example identifies the first proof step that must change.
body.consumer: It prevents a bounding package from certifying graph legality solely from preserved observational and query moments.
